title: Magnetic Screw Mat — What a screw mat does
description: A magnetic screw mat is a silicone work surface with magnets underneath and a dry-erase grid on top: screws park in labeled zones instead of rolling away. It turns teardowns from screw roulette into an organized procedure.

title: Magnetic Screw Mat — The magnetic layer
description: Magnets under the silicone hold steel screws firmly enough to survive a bumped bench but loosely enough to pick up with tweezers. Non-magnetic screws — brass standoffs, aluminum — still need their zones; the mat holds them by habit, not force.

title: Magnetic Screw Mat — Phone repair
description: Phone teardowns live or die on screw tracking: twenty tiny screws of four lengths, and one long screw in a short hole kills a board. The mat gives each length its own labeled cell, which is cheap insurance against a dead phone.

title: Magnetic Screw Mat — Common mistakes
description: The classic mistake is parking screws without labeling the zone, which produces a mat of mystery metal. The other is mixing lengths in one cell — the mat cannot organize what you refuse to separate.

title: Magnetic Screw Mat — Teardown workflow
description: The ritual: lay out the mat, draw the zones, number the steps, then remove screws into their zones in order. Reassembly reverses the film, and the leftover-inspection zone should be empty at the end.
